extracted.intended_audience: novelists, fiction writers, and critics or students studying the craft of the novel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on shaping a novel's form so it serves a single, expressive subject: choosing point of view, grouping scenes, rendering time and space, and avoiding intrusive commentary or wasted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and subject must coincide
rubrics_metrics.description: The best form is that which makes the most of its subject — the book in which the subject and the form coincide and are indistinguishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is disagreement between form and subject, there is stuff that is superfluous or stuff that is wanting; the form must express all the matter. Example (anti-pattern): War and Peace is criticised for a form that fails to do justice to its idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single, expressible subject / unity
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject, one and whole and irreducible — a novel cannot begin to take shape till it has this for its support. If it cannot be put into a phrase it is no subject for a novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The size or complexity of a subject is not the limitation — it must nonetheless be expressible concisely (the author suggests 'ten words' as a test). Until the subject is known there is nothing to be said of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a centre / avoid conflicting designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid a confusion of two designs; the novel should have a centre and a scheme that gathers its elements into a unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should devise a scheme that includes their distinct elements or else risk a book without a centre. Anti-pattern: allowing two separate themes to run without attempting to unify them (the critic's charge against Tolstoy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of material (avoid wastefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not be wasteful of the subject — a loose, unstructural form injures the story by importing irrelevant material or failing to use material for the book's purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism of a novel often rests on how much potential value is lost by poor structural decisions. Use material wholly for the purpose of the subject; avoid diverging into unrelated strands that dilute the main theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid authorial pamphleteering / explanatory interruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inserting interminable chapters of comment and explanation in the manner of a controversial pamphlet which interrupt the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such interruptions encourage readers to skip (example: sections where 'the historians' are mentioned). Prefer integrating thematic or philosophical material into the story rather than halting the narrative for exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and appropriate point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose and maintain an appropriate predominant point of view rather than shifting or 'choosing an onlooker at random'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point of view shapes the general effect; inconsistency fragments the book. Use a consistent narrator or method of observation so scenes cohere around the chosen perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use indirectness via onlooker perspective at critical moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach great public events or wide themes through the mind of an onlooker, borrowing the value of indirectness and the increased effect of a story seen mirrored in another's mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirectness can heighten effect — for high moments, choose an appropriate onlooker (Napoleon, Kutusov, a child at the stove, etc.). But select onlookers deliberately and consistently, not at random.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let the story tell itself / minimise authorial intrusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong novelist makes a story tell itself; avoid intruding with excessive authorial comment, explanation, or 'pamphleteering'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing is preferable to telling. Excessive authorial exposition reduces the narrative's immediacy and prompts readers to disengage. Reserve authorial voice for moments where it genuinely enhances understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a convincing sense of space and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Render an open world or a bounded horizon appropriate to the fable so characters feel to inhabit our world rather than a self-contained story-book realm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the fable needs an expansive, continuous world (Tolstoy) or an enclosed, intense setting (Dostoevsky). The chosen spatial treatment should support the novel's representative aims and sense of life beyond the book's immediate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render the passage of time through the book's structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of time is to be represented; it is more than a series of events in order — the lines and masses of the book must show time's movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length alone won't convey time. Make both the uninterrupted lapse of years and the cyclic rise-and-fall (the segment of a larger cycle) perceptible through the book's shape, scene grouping, and structural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show both continuous lapse and cyclical sweep of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time has two aspects: steady progression (years accumulating) and the rise-and-fall of a curve (the cycle of generations); both must be made apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the narrative gives the sense of time passing in faces, gestures, character change, and also that the chosen stretch is a recognisable segment of a larger cycle — the form must make this visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: True, consistent characterisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must remain absolutely true to themselves; wherever we meet them they should be the same persons, even while they change with time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency of character anchors readers amidst wandering plots. Even as characters age or mutate under conditions, retain their essential sameness so they remain believable and representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group and compose scenes to serve the central point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes must be properly grouped and composed to complete the book and support the principal point of view rather than constituting loosely related fragments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor grouping leads to a broken, fragmentary cycle. Compose episodes so they cumulatively serve the subject and reinforce the chosen perspective; avoid well-handled but misaligned fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the climax gathers and resolves the threads
rubrics_metrics.description: A good novel brings its story to a close in an episode which gathers up all the threads and winds them together, giving final shape to the characters' lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the ending to assemble narrative strands and produce a sense of finality appropriate to the subject; an ending that merely halts without unifying leaves the reader doubtful about the book's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve representative or universal quality over parochial particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a character's value is representative (universality), avoid converting them into the heroine of a merely particular domestic story that throws away their larger value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of over-focusing on particular plot details (e.g., which person a heroine marries) when the character's representative role is the novel's primary concern; such shifts can reduce the book's thematic scope.
